messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 421 — Hosted API latency spike detected. 90th percentile > 500ms for last 5m. paging: @oncall
tara: grabbing this now — seeing elevated p95 across gateway and model-pool. Looks like a queue buildup on model-pool-a.
samir: on my way, ETA ~3m. are we paged for user impact or internal alerts only?
tara: customer-facing timeouts for some heavy-gen requests — customer reports on #support. I'm still primary for the cycle but need to hand off in 8m for shift end. Samir, can you take driver when you arrive? I'll be comms for the handoff window.
samir: I can take driver. once i confirm the blocker i'll own the mitigation and rollbacks. josh, can you be secondary? Might need help with canary routing.
josh: available, will standby. if we need to re-route to smaller model variants I can flip the routing policy.
tara: quick notes: runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hosted-api-latency — start with model-pool backlog check + prefix cache hitrate. commands i've run:
```
# check pool queue
kubectl -n inference exec -it gateway-123 -- curl localhost:2020/metrics | grep "model_pool_queue"
# tail model-pool logs
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-pool-a --since=10m | tail -n 200
```
I saw repeated OOM attempts and a steady climb in queued requests for model-pool-a.
samir: confirmed. model-pool-a nodes 3/5 at very high memory; autoscaler not adding new nodes due to quota errors in us-west-2. seeing these events in node-provisioner: "quota exceeded". suspect cloud quota bump needed or temporary routing to replica pool-b.
tara: noted coverage gap: we have a maintenance window on the infra quotas scheduled right now (ops change) — that likely prevented autoscaler. I've messaged infra-ops in #eng-infra but they might be slow.
samir: plan: 1) fail open routing to model-pool-b (lower-capacity variant) 2) scale down heavy batch jobs, 3) request emergency quota increase with infra-ops. I'll start 1 and 2 now. tara — please take comms to update support and affected customers during the handoff. include ETA and mitigation.
tara: will do. posting to #support and creating a status update draft. will ping infra-ops for quota and escalate to oncall manager if no reply in 5m. draft status: "We are routing some requests to alternate inference pool to recover latency. No data loss. More updates in 10m." :warning:
samir: executing routing change: `redwoodctl route set --from model-pool-a --to model-pool-b --ratio 0.5` starting now.
ops-bot: ACTION: route update applied to 50% of traffic to model-pool-b by samir at 1737654375.
josh: monitoring downstream latency after routing flip. initial p95 dropping from 520ms -> 310ms on partial route. good sign.
tara: handoff: i'm offshift in 6m. Samir you are now primary driver. i'm comms owner for the transition and will remain available for 10m overlap. Josh is secondary. if infra-ops doesn't respond in 5m i escalate to infra-manager @leah.
samir: received, taking driver. i'll post updates here and in #incidents. thanks tara for the quick triage. digging further into autoscaler failure now.
tara: one more note — runbook step 4 mentions prefix cache warm-up after route flips. josh pls run the warmup script once p95 under 350ms: `python tools/prefix_warmup.py --targets model-pool-b --workers 10`
josh: got it. will run warmup once stable.
samir: tracking actions: [driver=samir], [comms=tara], [secondary=josh], [action: route -> model-pool-b], [escalate infra if no quota response]
tara: thanks team — i'll post a concise status to #ops-status and close my handoff once samir confirms stable. :thumbsup:
samir: update 1737654449 — p95 stabilized ~290ms across mixed routing. continuing monitoring and following up with infra-ops for quota fix. will take it from here and file a post-incident note for root-cause (autoscaler quota + maintenance overlap).
